data.title: Credentials Stored in Group Policy Preferences
data.summary:
Group Policy Preference files stored on the SYSVOL share contained passwords
encrypted with a publicly published key, allowing any authenticated domain user
to recover them in plaintext.
data.description:
Group Policy Preferences allow administrators to configure local accounts,
scheduled tasks, mapped drives, and services across the domain. Where a password
is supplied, it is stored in an XML file within the SYSVOL share in a field named
cpassword, encrypted using AES with a static key.

Microsoft published this key in 2012 alongside the MS14-025 update, meaning the
encryption provides no protection. Any account able to read SYSVOL - which by
design includes every authenticated user in the domain - can retrieve the file
and decrypt the password instantly using publicly available tooling.

Although the update prevents the creation of new preferences containing
passwords, it does not remove files created before it was applied. These files
therefore persist indefinitely unless explicitly located and deleted.

Files of this type were identified within the SYSVOL share, containing recoverable
credentials for local administrative accounts.
data.impact:
Any authenticated domain user could recover credentials for local administrator
accounts deployed across the estate. Because such accounts are frequently
configured identically on every host, a single recovered password commonly grants
administrative access to a large number of systems, enabling widespread lateral
movement and the extraction of further credential material from memory.
data.recommendation:
1. Search the SYSVOL share across all domain controllers for XML files containing
   the cpassword attribute and delete every file identified.

2. Change the password of every account exposed in this way, and review those
   accounts for evidence of prior unauthorised use.

3. Deploy Windows LAPS to manage local administrator passwords, which assigns a
   unique randomly generated password per host and rotates it automatically.

4. Ensure the MS14-025 update is applied to all systems used to author Group
   Policy, preventing new preferences containing passwords from being created.

5. Establish a recurring audit of SYSVOL content, as restored backups and
   migrated policies can reintroduce affected files after remediation.
